messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-4765 fired — service=az5-nic-link-flap, severity=P1, triggered at 4765432100
incident-bot: paging rotation: sre-oncall@pagerduty -> maria

maria: acking the page, I'm on it. spinning up graphs now.

pagerduty: maria acknowledged the page (INC-4765)

maria: quick snapshot: packet_loss spike seen across az5 egress interfaces, current ~6.3% sustained for 2m.
jonathan: seeing synthetic probes fail for endpoints routed to az5, 5xx rate +300% over baseline.
support_lead: support intake shows ~15 customers reporting session drops in EU, top tickets #4231 #4232 #4238.

sre-oncall: netops, any scheduled work or recent config push to fabric in az5?
netops: negative on schedules. telemetry shows RX errors and CRCs on multiple ToR uplinks in az5. no config change.

eli: sounds like a hardware/link-level issue. recommend diverting traffic away from az5 while we triage.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: az-nic-flap -> Step 1: Assess -> Step 2: Isolate -> Step 3: Divert traffic -> Step 4: Repair hardware

maria: starting isolation: cordoning suspicious nodes in az5 and marking them drainable. running:
```bash
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l zone=az5 -o name); do kubectl cordon $n; kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; done
```

maria: initiating routing policy 'az5-fallback-v2' to divert traffic gradually (10% -> 30% -> 100%).
jonathan: reroute in progress, watching error rates and latencies.

pagerduty: Incident severity elevated to SEV1 due to multi-tenant impact and customer errors.

rachel: net-hardware team looped in, standing by for inspect. asking for switch counters and NIC firmware versions.
netops: switch counters attached: ports 48/1-48/6 show intermittent link flaps and CRC errors. likely NIC/firmware on hosts, or SFP intermittency.

eli: starting divert now to az3: executing reroute-inflight --src=az5 --dst=az3 --step=gradual
ops-runbook-bot: automated step executed: traffic diverted 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 9 minutes per policy 'az-fallback-gradual'.

maria: confirm: at 30% divert packet_loss az5 down to ~2.1%, customer 5xxs down ~60%. continuing to 100%.

support_lead: updating status page and contacting top impacted customers with ETA for mitigation. :phone:
jonathan: end-to-end checks: most synthetic routes now passing; latency for diverted routes within SLOs.

netops: on physical inspection, a vendor NIC on a rack showed repeated link retrains; vendor confirmed known firmware edge-case. planning spare ASIC swap if flapping persists.
rachel: ordering replacement parts and scheduling patch window; will coordinate maintenance with eng-sre.

eli: enabling automatic fallback until hardware replaced to prevent re-blast. added a temporary policy to route affected prefixes to az3 permanently for the short term.

maria: divert complete at 04:12 UTC, traffic for affected prefixes now 100% on az3. monitoring...
jonathan: error rates returned to baseline within ~7 minutes of full divert. no new customer reports in last 10m.

support_lead: tally: ~15 customers initially affected, all acknowledged outreach; no escalations yet. drafting formal comms.

maria: marking incident as 'monitoring' — mitigation in place (traffic divert). next steps: hardware replacement, firmware update, postmortem/RCA. handing to morning oncall for long-term follow-up. :white_check_mark:
eli: recommended RCA items: root cause analysis of NIC firmware, review routing failover automation, ensure canary thresholds fine-grained.
ops-runbook-bot: follow-up ticket created: INC-4765-FOLLOWUP with checklist for hardware swap and firmware patch.

incident-bot: Incident INC-4765 moved to 'monitoring' state by maria (4765432167)
